title: Air Traffic Control — Coordinate Mission

learningOutcomes.text: Locate and plot a point from an ordered pair (x, y), moving along x first and then y.
Identify the quadrant of a point from the signs of its coordinates.
Interpret negative coordinates as movement to the left or downward.
Compare and order points by their x-coordinates.

premise: You are the air traffic controller. Flights radio in with coordinates, and you guide each aircraft across an airfield laid out on a coordinate grid.
progression: Starts with the target marked and a live coordinate readout, then removes the marker, then accepts any point in a quadrant, and finishes by ordering aircraft by x-coordinate.
assessment: Every scene is checked with a deterministic rule (exact point, quadrant, matches or order). Feedback names common mistakes such as swapped coordinates or sign errors, and hints become more explicit after each attempt.

assetNeeds.description: The aircraft the learner guides (from slide 7)

accessibility: Every move works with arrow keys, on-screen buttons, or by selecting a grid point — no dragging required.
Feedback uses text and icons, never color alone.
Respects the reduced-motion setting and starts sound only after the learner presses Start.

unresolvedDecisions.question: Include the distance-formula extension (slide 8) as optional practice?

assumptions: Grade 9 learners already know negative numbers on a number line.
Learners play individually on a laptop or tablet.
mechanicFit: The lesson is about locating positions from ordered pairs, so moving an aircraft to a coordinate makes learners perform exactly the skill being taught: move along x, then along y. A matching scene and an ordering scene check the related quadrant and comparison ideas without switching to a generic quiz.

scenes.title: Welcome to the tower
scenes.objective: Recognize the axes, the origin and what an ordered pair means.
scenes.visibleContent: A concept card over a small coordinate grid with three short points about the axes and ordered pairs.
scenes.learnerAction: Read the three points and continue.
scenes.expectedResult: The learner moves on to the first navigation task.
scenes.instruction: Your airfield is a coordinate grid.

points: The x-axis runs left to right; the y-axis runs bottom to top.
An ordered pair (x, y) means: move along x first, then along y.

scenes.errorFeedback: Read the three points, then choose Start mission.

scenes.title: Taxi to Runway Alpha
scenes.objective: Move to a point given as an ordered pair, x first then y.
scenes.visibleContent: Airfield grid from −5 to 5 across and −4 to 4 up; flight NX7 at the origin; Runway Alpha marked at (3, 2).
scenes.learnerAction: Move the aircraft with the arrow buttons, arrow keys or by selecting a grid point, then confirm.
scenes.instruction: Guide flight NX7 to Runway Alpha at (3, 2).
scenes.successFeedback: Cleared to land! (3, 2) is 3 right and 2 up.
scenes.errorFeedback: Check the order: move along x first, then along y.

scenes.title: Which quadrant?
scenes.objective: Identify a point's quadrant from the signs of its coordinates.
scenes.visibleContent: Six aircraft position cards and five bays: Quadrant I, II, III, IV and On an axis.
scenes.learnerAction: Drag each card into a bay, or select a card and then a bay.
scenes.expectedResult: Every position is in its correct quadrant; (0, 4) is on an axis.
scenes.instruction: Sort each aircraft position into its quadrant.
scenes.errorFeedback: Look at the signs: x tells left (−) or right (+), y tells down (−) or up (+).
hints: Quadrant I has both coordinates positive.
Quadrant II: x negative, y positive. Quadrant IV: x positive, y negative.
A zero coordinate puts the point on an axis.
scenes.completion: All six cards are in a correct bay.

scenes.title: Hangar check
scenes.objective: Use negative coordinates to locate a point without a marker.
scenes.visibleContent: The same airfield grid, no target marker; flight QF2 at the origin.
scenes.learnerAction: Move the aircraft to (−4, −3) and confirm.
scenes.instruction: Park flight QF2 at the hangar: (−4, −3).
scenes.errorFeedback: Check the signs: negative x is left, negative y is down.
hints: Negative x means left of the y-axis.
Move 4 units left, then 3 units down.
Both coordinates are negative, so the hangar is in Quadrant III.

scenes.title: Holding pattern
scenes.objective: Apply quadrant signs to choose any valid point.
scenes.visibleContent: The airfield grid; flight BA9 starts at (2, −1).
scenes.learnerAction: Move the aircraft to any point in Quadrant II and confirm.
scenes.expectedResult: The aircraft ends with negative x and positive y.
scenes.instruction: Park flight BA9 anywhere in Quadrant II.
scenes.successFeedback: Holding in Quadrant II — negative x, positive y.
scenes.errorFeedback: Quadrant II is top left: x must be negative and y positive.
hints: Quadrant II is the top-left part of the grid.
x must be negative and y must be positive.
For example, (−2, 2) is in Quadrant II.
scenes.completion: The aircraft is confirmed in Quadrant II.

scenes.title: Line up for take-off
scenes.visibleContent: Five aircraft cards with their positions, to be arranged in a row.
scenes.learnerAction: Arrange the cards from left (smallest x) to right (largest x).
scenes.expectedResult: Cards ordered by x; the two with x = 1 may be in either order.
scenes.instruction: Line up the aircraft from left to right by x-coordinate.
scenes.successFeedback: Lined up and ready for take-off!
scenes.errorFeedback: Compare the first number of each pair: a smaller x goes further left.
hints: Only the x-coordinate (the first number) matters.
Negative x values go furthest left.
QF2 and BA9 both have x = 1, so either order is fine.
scenes.completion: All five cards are in a correct order.
